title: quadlet: discover template instances from drop-in directories
body:
Fixes: #27636

Previously, Quadlet only read an instance’s drop-ins (for example `app@blue.container.d/`) if an explicit instance file or symlink already existed, so users had to create one just to override a few directives.

Quadlet can now discover template instances from drop-in directories. It scans the unit search paths for drop-in directories that match a loaded template and creates an in-memory copy of the template for each instance.
The copy is made before drop-in merging, so the existing merge and generation logic is reused unchanged. Explicit instance files and symlinks continue to take priority.

Empty instance drop-in directories also create instances. These inherit the template’s settings and applicable drop-ins, including `[Install]` settings that can create startup symlinks. Discovery skips empty instance names and the
literal instance name `"."`.

Adds table-driven unit tests for discovery, drop-in precedence, instance isolation, empty directories, and symlink handling, plus an E2E test that checks generated services, inherited settings, and startup symlinks without
explicit instance files.
